story.system_instruction: Create a concise social-video storyboard from only the user's approved story and assets. Divide the story into three-second shots with one clear meaning and one principal action per shot. Preserve the user's source language for story text, dialogue, and narration. Keep all work-specific characters, dialogue, ending, locations, and sound-effect timing in the work data, never in the shared production profile. Plan the first frame, continuity source, camera, lighting, emotion, dialogue, audio, and nine-frame review points for every shot. Do not proceed from storyboard planning to video generation before the user reviews and explicitly approves the official Excel storyboard.
requirements: Lead with a visually clear hook suitable for a short social video, without inventing claims that are absent from the user's story.
Use 10 to 14 three-second shots for a target duration of 30 to 42 seconds.
Give each shot one principal action, one camera intention, and one continuity decision.
Keep dialogue and narration short enough to fit within the configured maximum speech duration.
State whether each shot starts from its storyboard image or the previous shot's verified final frame.
Describe all visible subjects, composition, action, expression, camera, lighting, and continuity explicitly.
Plan nine observable review moments per shot at three frames per second.
Do not add work-specific people, dialogue, endings, logos, or sound-effect timestamps unless they are present in the user's work data.
Build the official Excel storyboard and wait for explicit human approval before any video-generation request.
story.audience: People who want to create a memorable social-media video with step-by-step AI-agent assistance
story.prompt_language_instruction: Write main image prompts and video prompts in clear English while preserving exact proper nouns supplied by the user.
story.output_language_instruction: Write storyboard explanations, dialogue, and narration in the same language as the user's source story unless the user explicitly requests another language.

requirements: Generate one cinematic keyframe that matches the selected aspect ratio; do not create a collage or split screen.
Treat approved character references as identity constraints for face, body proportions, materials, colors, costume, and silhouette.
Show only the characters required by the current shot, even when a reference image contains additional subjects.
Preserve the shot's specified camera, subject positions, lighting, environment, and space for later subtitles.
Do not reproduce text, captions, interfaces, logos, watermarks, or unrelated franchise elements found in references.
Keep identity, environment, camera axis, props, and lighting consistent with adjacent storyboard shots.
Generate exactly one three-second 720p, 24fps shot from the approved starting image and prompt.
Preserve character identity, component count, costume, color, proportions, environment, and camera direction throughout the shot.
Use one principal action with physically readable motion and avoid unrequested cuts, morphs, new subjects, text, logos, or camera jumps.
When continuity is required, use the verified final frame of the preceding shot as the next starting frame.
Treat inline negative terms as prohibitions inside the main prompt because this API family has no separate negative-prompt field.
Ignore generated audio from the video model in the final production and create approved dialogue, narration, ambience, music, and effects separately.
Extract and inspect nine real frames before accepting a generated shot.
reference_instructions: Use storyboard_image for a new scene, time, location, composition, or deliberate reset.
Use previous_final_frame only when the same scene and motion should continue across the three-second boundary.
Use the starting image as the authoritative composition and character references only for identity and approved design traits.
Limit character identity references to the declared maximum and prefer the fewest authoritative references needed.
Do not use private or unlicensed references, and never upload a secret or personal identifier as a reference.

audio.default_speaker: A clear, composed general-purpose narrator; work-specific characters may override the voice in work data after user review.
audio.default_style: Speak naturally and clearly at a calm social-video pace. Preserve the intended emotion without shouting, rushing, adding words, or altering the approved dialogue.
audio.tts_language_instruction: Read dialogue and narration in the same language as the approved source text, preserving names and intended pronunciation.
audio.transcription_instruction: Transcribe only the speech that is actually audible, in its original language, without translating, summarizing, correcting, or inventing missing words.
